SUCCESSION
Before and after
THE REALM
Damascus and the places of the account
Aram (Syria). Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
The LORD delivered Israel “into the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael, all their days”. 2 Kings 13:3
“So Hazael king of Syria died; and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his stead.” 2 Kings 13:24

“Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz took again out of the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael the cities, which he had taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father by war. Three times did Joash beat him.” 2 Kings 13:25
Amos: “I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, which shall devour the palaces of Ben-hadad.” Amos 1:4
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Israel's cities taken in Jehoahaz's days were recovered from him by Jehoash. 2 Kings 13:25
“The children of Israel dwelt in their tents, as beforetime.” 2 Kings 13:5
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
PROPHETS
The prophets who spoke about him
El Elisha “thou shalt smite Syria but thrice”
Am Amos “which shall devour the palaces of Ben-hadad”
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
FROM SCRIPTURE, ON THE MAIN SYSTEM'S DATES
He followed Hazael, who oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz (died 798 BC on Thiele, McFall and Young); Jehoash of Israel (798–782 BC) beat him three times. When his reign ended is not known.
Adad-nirari III of Assyria
T. Nicol, ISBE (1915), “Benhadad” and “Hazael”
Nicol takes the saviour to be the Assyrian king whose capture of Damascus crippled Syria, so that Jehoash could recover Israel's cities. 2 Kings 13:5 [15][16]
Jehoash and Jeroboam II

Keil finds the saviour in Jehoahaz's two successors: Jehoash, who took back the cities, and Jeroboam, who restored Israel's borders. He reports and rejects other answers: an angel, Elisha, one of Joash's captains, and Jeroboam alone (Thenius). 2 Kings 13:25 2 Kings 14:25 [22]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 3
2 Kings 13 2 Kings 14 Amos 1
PASSAGES · 4
2 Kings 13:3–7 2 Kings 13:14–25 2 Kings 14:28 Amos 1:3–5
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no length of reign and does not tell how his reign ended.
Scripture does not name Adad-nirari III or any “Mari’”; the identification is a modern one.
Kings says Jeroboam son of Joash later “recovered Damascus” (2 Kings 14:28) but names no king of Damascus.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textBen-hadad the son of Hazael (2 Kings 13:3, 24–25); not the earlier Ben-hadads of Asa's and Elisha's days. 2 Kings 13:3 2 Kings 13:24

Scholars' viewT. Nicol (ISBE, 1915) identifies him with “Mari’”, the king of Damascus in Adad-nirari III's inscriptions, and says this “is now generally believed”; Mari’ “means in Aramaic ‘lord’”.[15]
